title: Acclivity Health inference intake field diary
content:
Meeting summary (2025-11-03, 11:00 PT) with Acclivity Health — intake and technical alignment. Attendees: Sofia Park (Redwood), Maya Singh (Redwood), Dr. Priya Patel (Acclivity CTO), Omar Hammad (Acclivity SRE), Lisa Chen (Acclivity Privacy). Goal: capture constraints for a Private deployment proof-of-concept to serve clinical triage assistant (async + sync assistants).

High-level asks from Acclivity: 
- Private deployment inside customer VPC (no egress to public internet from model hosts). Control plane can be managed by Redwood but must support customer-controlled KMS/HSM and audit logs.
- Data classification: PHI may be present in request payloads. They need configurable redaction triggers + on-host transient cache only, with automatic TTL purge and audit trail.
- Latency & throughput targets: target p95 latency <= 200ms for 512-token responses in normal traffic; expected steady state 35–50 RPS with spikes to 120 RPS during shift changes.
- Model quality: clinical-safe responses, high factuality. Preference for open models we can run privately (weight constraints discussed below).
- Compliance: SOC2 + regional requirements; logs must be forwarded to their Splunk instance with field-level masking for PHI.

Notes / technical constraints discussed: 
1) Network & infra:
   - VPC peering vs customer-provisioned VPN: Acclivity prefers VPC peering inside AWS account; asked for minimal cross-account IAM roles.
   - Private control plane: they want option to self-host the control plane components in a private subnet (air-gapped not required for POC).
   - Egress rules: model nodes must not allow outbound connections except to internal telemetry collectors. Need an init script we can audit that enforces no outbound shell access.

2) Keys & encryption:
   - Must integrate with their AWS KMS and optional external HSM for key wrapping of model keys and TLS certs.
   - Disk encryption at rest and ephemeral NVMe cache encryption. KV-cache must be encrypted with customer KMS key and keys rotated every 30 days.

3) Model & runtime considerations:
   - Preferred model family: efficient 7B–20B variants for inference footprint. Clinical hallucination risk flagged — propose running eval suite (1000-case clinical prompts) as part of onboarding and compare 3 model candidates.
   - Quantization: they are open to int8 quantized models if we can show no degradation on the clinical evals. Emphasize we should keep a float32 baseline for canary.
   - GPU selection: Acclivity asked about H100 vs A100 tradeoffs. Notes: H100 gives better throughput for 70B+ models and attention kernel speedups; A100 is acceptable for 7B–20B if cost is a concern. For POC recommend A100d with 80GB if budget-limited; plan for H100 testing if we move to dedicated.
   - KV cache sizing: typical patient conversation ~5–8 turns, avg tokens 300/session. Need to ensure host memory for ~10k concurrent KV entries in peak spike.

4) Performance/levers we discussed:
   - Batching: Redwood's batching policy will help reduce tokens/cost but must not increase tail latency above SLO. Propose single-request priority queue for triage-high traffic routes and aggressive batching for low-priority background jobs (summarization, embeddings).
   - Prefix caching: many prompts have identical system instructions. Suggest enabling prefix cache to save compute on repeated templates (ops note: need to ensure cache does not store PHI).

5) Observability & logging:
   - Full request/response tracing for debugging but PHI redaction must be applied before logs leave the model host. They require per-token cost and latency breakdowns for a sample of requests.
   - Alerting thresholds: p95 latency > 250ms, error rate > 1.5% for 5m window.

6) Data flow & privacy gotchas (explicit items to track):
   - Redaction edge case: partial PHI in system prompt vs user prompt — need clear precedence (user-provided redaction tokens should override system).
   - Third-party telemetry: telemetry endpoints must be configurable; default must be disabled for POC.
   - Model artifacts: customer insists model weights are stored only on customer-controlled storage; provisioning flow must stream weights directly into model hosts without staging in Redwood-managed buckets.

Open questions captured during call: 
- What level of throughput do they expect for embedding generation (used for search/triage) vs token-gen? (Action: Omar to provide typical monthly QPS for embeddings by 2025-11-06.)
- Will they accept int8 quantization for the clinical model if we provide a fallback float32 canary? (Action: Acclivity legal & clinical ops to sign off after eval; Lisa to confirm by 2025-11-10.)
- Audit log retention window required: 12 months min? (Action: Priya to confirm exact retention and retention-at-rest requirements.)

Immediate risks / gotchas: 
- If we attempt to cache prompts containing PHI we risk compliance breach. Need explicit engineering constraint: cache only on normalized system templates and hashed non-PHI user tokens (or disable caching for endpoints flagged PHI).
- KV cache eviction behavior can surface patient identifiers if we snapshot memory for debugging. Plan to never snapshot full-memory outside the host; debugging dumps must be scrubbed.
- Sizing underestimation: 120 RPS burst with 512 token responses could saturate a single A100 cluster. We should model cost and concurrency (estimate: ~2–3 A100 80GB nodes per 50 RPS for 20B model w/ modest batching).

Proposed POC scope and success criteria (draft): 
- Deploy Redwood Private POC into Acclivity AWS account with VPC peering and customer KMS integration.
- Run three candidate models through clinical eval set; pass means: top model must have F1 >= baseline on symptom extraction and hallucination rate <= 3% (metrics to be defined in eval doc).
- Meet latency SLO: p95 <= 250ms for 512-token responses in steady traffic (35–50 RPS).
- Demonstrate log forwarding with field-level masking and show audit trail for 30 days.
- Cost telemetry: provide per-route token cost estimates and weekly cost report.

Immediate next steps (owners + due dates): 
- Omar (Acclivity) to share monthly QPS and embeddings workload sample by 2025-11-06.
- Maya (Redwood) to open infra provisioning ticket RED-1782 and add initial OIDC/IAM role draft by 2025-11-07.
- Sofia (Redwood) to schedule follow-up deep-dive on model selection and eval harness with Priya & clinical SME for 2025-11-10.
- Carlos (Redwood) to produce a short tech-runbook draft for "no-egress" enforcement and ephemeral key rotation, link in CONF-ACCL-21 by 2025-11-09.
- Lisa (Acclivity) to confirm audit retention and legal signoff on log redaction policy by 2025-11-10.

Misc notes / ideas we sketched: 
- Consider a two-path provisioning flow: POC uses a lightweight, infra-as-code blue-green with pinned model bundle; production uses dedicated GPU pool with canary rollout and automatic rollback on QA metric regression.
- Keep an explicit "PHI-safe" endpoint flag that disables caching and sampling for any route labeled as PHI. Could be enforced at the API gateway.
- Add an eval that checks redaction efficacy: automated prompts that include synthetic PHI tokens and verify no tokens leak in logs/telemetry.

End of intake. This doc is the working diary — rough, chronological. Will refine into a customer-facing POC brief once we confirm the three open items.

Raw action log (timestamps local PT):
- 2025-11-03 10:58: call connected
- 2025-11-03 11:42: agreed POC scope sketch
- 2025-11-03 12:10: wrap (follow-up invites sent)

Short checklist for next internal sync: 
- [ ] Run a quick cost model for A100 vs H100 for 20B and 70B candidates (Carlos)
- [ ] Draft eval pass criteria and build small synthetic PHI leak test (Sofia + Maya)
- [ ] Prepare VPC peering runbook and minimal IAM role templates (Maya)
- [ ] Draft customer-facing POC brief for review (Sofia)

Notes-to-self: keep the POC minimal surface area. Focus on proving compliance-safe ops and predictable latency. Keep telemetry optional until legal signs off.
